subject: QuantaHealth renewal uplift & co-term coordination
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <procurement@quantahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Mid-contract uplift + co-term ask / QH budget window

Karthik,

Quick note from procurement at QuantaHealth — we had a spike in usage for PatientAssist in Oct and our finance team wants to lock in additional committed capacity for the next two quarters. We’re mid-contract (ends 2027-03-31) and want to: 1) add a mid-contract uplift for immediate capacity through Dec, and 2) co-term the uplift to align with our existing renewal date.

Key constraints:
- Need a pricing footprint and PO-ready number by 11/12 to hit our internal purchase window.
- Budget owner is on a hard freeze for incremental recurring spend; a one-time credit or invoice smoothing would help procurement secure approval.
- Legal will need a short amendment rather than a full MSA re-sign.

Can you share what flexibility you have on uplift discounts, any short-term smoothing, and an estimated timeline for amendment? Happy to set a quick call if useful.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Procurement Manager — QuantaHealth
procurement@quantahealth.com

Attachment: usage_report_oct2026.csv (stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <procurement@quantahealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift + co-term ask / QH budget window

Samantha — thanks for the heads up and context. Appreciate the timeline. High level options we can move on quickly: 

1) One-time uplift (Q4 spike): add 30% additional capacity for Oct–Dec as a short-term uplift, invoiced in two installments. We can offer a 10% concession on uplift unit rates if PO received by 11/12.

2) Co-term + smoothing: convert uplift to a committed add-on that co-terms with your existing agreement (ends 2027-03-31). If you take the commit as annualized across remaining term we can offer a blended uplift rate with a 7% discount and invoice smoothing over the remaining months.

3) Bridge credit: For procurement constraints we can front a bridge credit covering 50% of the uplift cost to be reconciled at renewal (applies if you commit to an expanded baseline at renewal).

I’ve attached two quick artifacts: "QuantaHealth_MA_Pricing_Scenarios.pdf" with scenario math and a fillable "QH_mutual_action_plan.xlsx" you can use for internal signoffs.

Ask: can you confirm whether procurement needs the uplift as one-off spend (CapEx style) or recurring Opex so we price correctly? Also, what PO/approval code would you include so we can mark the quote?

Happy to jump on a 20-min call Thursday to run numbers with Lauren (billing) and Monica (CS) if that helps.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

Attachments: QuantaHealth_MA_Pricing_Scenarios.pdf (stub), QH_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (stub)

From: Samantha Lee <procurement@quantahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: QuantaHealth Legal <legal@quantahealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 12:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift + co-term ask / QH budget window

Thanks Karthik — that breakdown helps. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement preference: we need the uplift to look like a one-time committed purchase this quarter (internal capex carveout). If it can be structured as a one-time invoice with a smoothing/credit applied to renewal that would satisfy finance.
- Discount ask: given we’re moving quickly, can Redwood extend 15% off uplift unit rates if PO is received by 11/12? That gets our budget owner across the line.
- Legal: we will accept an amendment (SOW addendum) with the uplift and co-term language; they want a redline by 11/15.

If you can’t hit 15% across the board, would Redwood consider a two-tier concession: 12% guaranteed on the one-time uplift plus a performance rebate that brings effective discount to 15% if monthly committed usage stays >= 110% of current baseline through Dec? That would be a compromise procurement and finance can live with.

DocuSign: please route the amendment to legal@quantahealth.com when ready.

Regards,
Samantha

Attachment: QH_budget_code_2026Q4.txt (stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <procurement@quantahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift + co-term ask / QH budget window

Samantha — thanks — appreciate the clear timeline. Internal check and proposal: 

- We can approve a one-time uplift priced as a single invoice if PO arrives by 11/12. Offering: 12% off uplift unit rates upfront + a conditional performance rebate that increases the effective discount to 15% if usage average >= 110% of your baseline during Nov–Dec (rebate applied at next invoice or as credit to renewal).

- Co-term: we’ll include co-term language in an amendment (short SOW addendum). Monica will draft the amendment and Lauren will confirm invoicing cadence and smoothing language. Expect a redline to you by 11/15 for legal.

- Bridge credit: we can also hold a $25k bridge credit on file to ease procurement; reconciled at renewal if you take the expanded baseline.

Next steps I’ll execute:
1) Monica to draft the SOW addendum and performance rebate clause.
2) Lauren to build the PO-ready quote with the 12% upfront concession + rebate line and invoice scheduling.
3) I’ll loop in legal if any non-standard contract language is required.

If that sounds acceptable, I’ll mark the HubSpot deal (QH-4521) and route the draft to legal@quantahealth.com for 11/15 redline.

Best,
Karthik
